podcast.title: Conservative Repertoire
podcast.body: Sting and Jerry Richardson grew frustrated with the band's conservative repertoire, desiring to play more modern rock-era jazz, which ultimately led them to form Last Exit. "Richardson and Sting had been frustrated by the Big Band's conservative repertoire and they wanted to play more modern rock-era jazz like Weather Report or Return to Forever."

podcast.title: Sting's Early Band
podcast.body: This jazz combo, named after Newcastle-on-Tyne (the nearest city to Sting's birthplace), was where a young Gordon Sumner played bass in the early 1970s. "This is the Newcastle Big Band, a jazz combo young Gordon Sumner played with in the early 70s. If you listen closely, that's him on the bass."
